mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 950K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST > 950K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7%, indicating a strong labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined effect boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 30% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals reduced supply chain pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from lower input costs.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of INDPRO on input costs
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 45% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2%, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days are positively correlated with the level of Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS), as increased spending boosts economic activity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly correlated with RSAFS levels (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, indicating a tightening monetary cycle, and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate accelerates above 3% over a quarter, the combined effect leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL growth > 3% over a quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% over two months, indicating labor market stress, leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of UNRATE on consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 1%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of Gross Domestic Product (GDPC1) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as increased economic output boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly correlated with GDPC1 levels (t-test p > 0.15).
